subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — possible SDK retransmit behavior
messages:
From: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@novacorp.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@novacorp.com
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — urgent

Hi Priyom / Monica,

We started seeing a large degradation this morning — ~15% of our requests to your hosted endpoint are 5xx or 429s, and overall P95 latency jumped from ~180ms to 1.6s. This began at ~08:40 PDT and has been intermittent but sustained. Our customers are complaining about timeouts.

Attached are two short syslog snippets and a small repro curl script that triggers a cascade when run at scale. Can someone confirm whether any config or runtime change was rolled on your side? If not, we suspect our recent SDK update may be involved.

We need a quick read: is this a capacity/backpressure issue on Redwood, or a retry-pattern problem on our client?

Thanks,
Elaine
Director, Integrations — NovaCorp

Attachments: novacorp-request-syslog-snippet.txt (text), repro-script.sh (shell)
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@novacorp.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:45:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — urgent

Hi Elaine — thanks for the logs and repro. We're looking. Can you confirm which SDK version you rolled last night and whether you enabled the new "aggressive-retry" flag? If you can paste the exact client config that would speed us up.

I'll triage with Markus (infra) and Monica (CS) and follow up within 45 minutes with a controlled read of ingress and quota metrics.

— Priyom
Senior SDR (Sales Eng) — Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:08:37 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — urgent

Pulling logs now. Quick summary from the control-plane: there were no deployment changes on our end during the window. However, our ingress shows a high spike of short-lived, repeated POSTs from a small set of client IPs for NovaCorp between 08:38–09:05. Many of those are hitting rate limits; a subset produced transient 5xx responses while the autoscaler spun up additional workers. The pattern looks like repeated retries with near-constant inter-request spacing — classic retry amplification.

I started a filtered trace for NovaCorp and captured the following: client retries with constant 200–300ms intervals and very little variance (no jitter). Server-side transient errors (backend RPC timeouts) then led to more immediate retries. We need to confirm the SDK defaults on NovaCorp's side.

Markus
Staff Engineer, Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@novacorp.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 11:02:04 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — urgent

Thanks Markus — we shipped SDK v3.4.1 at 02:10 PDT last night. The release notes say "improved reliability: faster retry default" — I didn't think to change interrupts. Our ops lead confirms the default retry backoff in that release is fixed 250ms for three attempts (no jitter). We're reverting to v3.3.8 now and will run the repro script scaled-down.

Elaine

--- Forwarded message ---
From: ops@novacorp.com
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 10:58:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK v3.4.1 release notes

SDK v3.4.1 default backoff: 250ms fixed x3, no jitter. Intended to reduce tail latency for single-client workloads.
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@novacorp.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 12:03:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — urgent

Elaine — thanks for confirming. Action plan from Redwood: 1) We recommend NovaCorp roll back to v3.3.8 (or set client backoff to exponential with jitter) — doing that should stop the retransmit spiral. 2) We'll apply a temporary routing throttle for requests originating from the affected IP range for the next 30 minutes to allow autoscaler catch-up and prevent cross-customer impact. 3) We'll run a short canary of ingress for NovaCorp and share trace snippets.

I'll coordinate the throttle window and timeline; Priyom will keep your execs updated.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@novacorp.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 15:40:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 — urgent

Quick exec note for visibility: Elaine, we've implemented a short throttle and your team switching to v3.3.8 (or enabling exponential+jitter) is the right immediate mitigation. We'll reserve a dedicated Dedicated hotspot for NovaCorp throughput testing tomorrow so you can validate without impacting production traffic.

Priyom/Monica — please follow up with a post-mortem doc and include suggested SDK default changes that would avoid "aggressive-retry" as a default in client libraries. I want to capture a recommendation for our SDK guidance and docs.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
